title: Reverse an Array
inputOutputContract: Input n followed by n values; output one space-separated line, blank if n=0.

mistakes.hint1: Inspect the duplicates swapped value behavior in reverseArray; the current algorithm is close, but one operation changes its result.
mistakes.hint2: Start by tracing T1 manually. Watch array indices / comparisons / loop boundaries / return values at each iteration or recursive return.
mistakes.hint3: Check the invariant of reverseArray: Swap the values at symmetric left and right indices until the pointers meet.
mistakes.hint4: Concentrate on the expression or branch that controls this mistake: `arr[right] = arr[left];`. What does it do on the failing input?
mistakes.hint5: Compare the intermediate state with the expected output of T1. The mistake is in duplicates swapped value, not merely formatting.
mistakes.hint6: Adjust the faulty operation so that it follows this rule: Swap the values at symmetric left and right indices until the pointers meet.
mistakes.hint7: A targeted correction is to replace `arr[right] = arr[left];` with `arr[right] = temp;` in reverseArray, then retest T1–T6.
